# Overview
## Analysis Overview
+ Replacement cost approach
+ Basin-level analysis (235 global river basins)

## The information we need and how to get them:
+ 1. Basin-level municipal water quantity (withdrawal volumes)
  + we can use (i) the FAO Aquastat data for 2019, (ii) basin_to_country_mapping.csv

+ 2. Source shares of municipal withdrawals: The share of the basin-level water withdrawal volumes for municipal water use by source (surface water, groundwater, desalinated water, etc.). 
  + subtract know desaslination where available   
 
+ 3. Cost information for alternative water sources (surface water, groundwater, desalinated water, etc.) by basin.

+ 4. Candidate replacement technologies for each basin (e.g., desalination, groundwater, etc.)
  + For example, desalination may be feasible for costal basins

# Data 

For the main data, we will use datasets from the Global Change Analysis Model (GCAM). The github repository for GCAM water data is [here](https://github.com/JGCRI/gcam-core/tree/master/input/gcamdata/inst/extdata/water). I installed the GCAM water data package, go to DownGit and paste the link to the water data folder in the GCAM repository.  


## Main datasets

### River basin information
+ **`basin_to_country_mapping.csv`** - Basin assigned to the country which has the largest basin area.
+ Geospatial boundary data for the 235 global river basins (i.e., gcam basin) is downloaded from [JGCRI Github repository for `gcammaptools` R package](https://github.com/JGCRI/gcammaptools/tree/master). The data is stored in `Raw/Boundary/gcam_235_basins.gpkg`.
+ NOTE: `GCAM_basin_id` in `basin_to_couinty_mapping.csv` and `region_id` in `gcam_235_basins.gpkg` can be used to link the two datasets.

+ 

### Domestic water use information
+ **`nonirrigation_withdrawal.csv`** - Nonirrigation withdrawal by country
+ **`resource_water_share.csv`** - Fresh and saline water share and consumption to withdrawal ratios based on 1995 US data.
+ **`municipal_water_use_efficiency.csv`** - The data here are computed as municipal water consumption / withdrawals for 7 global regions


### Cost information for alternative water sources

#### Surface water cost
+ **`xanthos_accessible_water.csv`** - Accessible runoff from Xanthos simulation (Units: km^3/yr, for 2061-2016). 


#### Disalination cost
+ **`A71.globaltech_cost.csv`** - Desalination non-energy costs (1975$ per cubic meter of desalinated water (1975$/m3))
+  **`DesalData_capacity_basin.csv`** - Desalinated water production capacity by basin
+  **`AusNWC_desal_techs.csv`** -  the technology shares of desalinated water production by continent.

#### Groundwater cost
+ **`superwell_groundwater_cost_elec_dls.csv`** 
  + Groundwater nonrenewable resource curves with capital costs disaggregated from electricity (pumping) requirements. Includes both energy and nonenergy costs. Costs and depth bins are processed from superwell output. elec_coef = electric_energy / (Well_Yield * Annual_Operation_time). 
  + costs in 1975USD per m3; available in km3; elec_coef in kwh per m3; depletion limits in percent
  + Link to the original study: 
    + [Niazi et al. 2025: Long-term hydro-economic analysis tool for evaluating global groundwater cost and supply: Superwell v1.1.](https://gmd.copernicus.org/articles/18/1737/2025/)
    + [Niazi et al. 2024: Globally Gridded Groundwater Extraction Volumes and Costs under Six Depletion and Ponded Depth Targets](https://www.osti.gov/biblio/2307832)
    + [Turner et al. 2019: "Influence of groundwater extraction costs and resource depletion limits on simulated global nonrenewable water withdrawals over the 21st century"](https://agupubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1029/2018EF001105)
    
+ 


### Water withdrawal data
+ The FAO Aquastat data in GCAM water data package only contains data up to 2017. More recent data was downloaded from the FAO Aquastat website. The following datasets were downloaded:
  + Municipal water withdrawal (2018-2022)   
  + Desalinated water produced (2018-2022)

# Data Overview

```{r}
#| eval: false 

# /*===========================================*/
#'=  Map of 235 major river-basins =
# /*===========================================*/
# --- Basin-country correspondence --- #
tbl_basin_to_country <- fread(here("Data/raw/gcam/water/basin_to_country_mapping.csv"))

# --- Country boundary --- #
ctry_bd <- st_read(here("Data/raw/Boundary/z_ee_r250_correspondence.gpkg"), quiet = TRUE)

# --- Basin boundary --- #
basin_bd <- st_read(here("Data/raw/Boundary/gcam_235_basins.gpkg"), quiet = TRUE)

# --- map of major river basin --- #
ggplot() +
  # geom_sf(data = ctry_bd, color = "red") +
  geom_sf(data = basin_bd, fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.5)

ggsave(
  here("Data/Results/Figures/map_basin.png"),
  width = 6,
  height = 4,
)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-map-basin
#| fig-cap: "Map of the 235 global river basins"

knitr::include_graphics(here("Data/Results/Figures/map_basin.png"))
```

## Cost & availability information for alternative water sources

```{r}

# --- Surface water (year: 1961 - 2016) --- #
sw_accessible_water <- fread(here("Data/Raw/gcam/water/xanthos_accessible_water.csv"))

# --- Groundwater (year: ?) --- #
gw_cost_elec_dls <- fread(here("Data/Raw/gcam/water/superwell_groundwater_cost_elec_dls.csv"))

# --- Desalination cost (1975$/m3)--- #
```
